lists.title: Parks, trails and outdoor walks in Port St. Lucie
lists.intro: Port St. Lucie has city parks, a state preserve and a county nature center with walking trails you can use today. Every place below has an official page that we read on 2026-10-27 for its address, hours or fees.

faq.q: Where can I find walking trails in Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: The City of Port St. Lucie lists about three miles of walking trails at Oak Hammock Park and a sidewalk trail system at Woodland Trails Park. Savannas Preserve State Park has multi-use trails shared by hikers, bicyclists and horseback riders, and Oxbow Eco-Center & Preserve trails are open sunrise to sunset daily per the county.

faq.q: Is there a fee to hike at Savannas Preserve State Park?
faq.a: Florida State Parks lists $3 per vehicle (up to eight people) and $2 per pedestrian, with the park open 8 a.m. to sunset. Fees can change, so check the state's hours-and-fees page before you go.

faq.q: Is there somewhere to walk in the evening?
faq.a: The Boardwalk at The Port District is listed by the city as open 24/7 and lighted, about 4,300 feet long. Jessica Clinton Park has a lighted half-mile sidewalk loop and is listed open until 10 p.m. (see the fitness list).

faq.q: Will the trails be wet?
faq.a: Florida State Parks warns that the Savannas trails wind through marsh, so depending on the season and weather they may be wet. Check conditions with the park office before you head out.

lists.title: Farmers markets and fresh, local food near Port St. Lucie
lists.intro: Port St. Lucie's regular Saturday and Sunday markets are in Fort Pierce, Tradition and the MIDFLORIDA Event Center. Market schedules change by season, so each entry below says only what its official or tourism page states.

faq.q: Is there a farmers market in Port St. Lucie on Sunday?
faq.a: Visit St. Lucie describes the Tradition Neighborhood Market as a Sunday market with fresh produce and handcrafted goods, and lists a Port St. Lucie Green Market at the MIDFLORIDA Event Center on November 15, 2026 from 12 to 6 p.m. Visit St. Lucie's guide does not give regular Sunday hours, so confirm the current schedule with the organizer.

faq.q: Is there a Saturday farmers market near Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: The Downtown Fort Pierce Farmers Market runs every Saturday, rain or shine, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. from October through May and 8 a.m. to noon from June through September, at 101 Melody Lane (Marina Square).

faq.q: Are the vendors at these markets organic?
faq.a: The Fort Pierce market describes its produce as farm-fresh and does not mention organic certification. If organic matters to you, ask each vendor directly.

faq.q: Do the markets run all year?
faq.a: The Fort Pierce market states it runs every Saturday, with different hours in summer. Visit St. Lucie's guide does not state a season for the other markets, so check before you travel.

lists.title: Free and low-cost fitness in Port St. Lucie
lists.intro: Port St. Lucie's city fitness centers charge $5 for an adult day pass, and the city's Fitness Parks Pass covers yoga, tai chi, Zumba and boot camps in parks from November through April. Free options are the outdoor fitness stations in city parks and group runs at a local running store.

faq.q: Is there free yoga in Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: The city's yoga in the parks is pass-based: $25 for 5 classes or $50 for 12 classes, plus tax. The city also runs occasional no-registration sample classes, such as a free tai chi class and a free Zumba class in July 2026, and its outdoor fitness stations are free to use.

faq.q: When do outdoor fitness classes start?
faq.a: The city says outdoor classes (yoga in the parks, tai chi, Zumba and boot camps) return from November through April. We could not find a published fall 2026 schedule on 2026-10-27, so call 772-204-7101.

faq.q: How much is a day pass at the city fitness centers?
faq.a: The city lists $5 for adults 18-59 and $4 for students 16+ with ID and seniors 60+, plus tax, with photo ID required. No one under 16 is admitted to the fitness centers.

faq.q: Is there a run club in Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: Fleet Feet Port St. Lucie lists a Monday group run for runners and walkers, 6:30 to 7:30 p.m. at 11586 SW Village Pkwy. Cost is not listed, so ask the store.

lists.title: Places to eat lighter in Port St. Lucie
lists.intro: These Port St. Lucie spots serve salads, bowls, wraps, juices or smoothies, and each one's own website shows its menu or hours. None paid to be listed and none are partners.

faq.q: Where can I find healthy food in Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: Menus on the businesses' own sites show salads, wraps, açaí or poke bowls, juices and smoothies at Berry Forkin' Good, 3Natives, Field of Greens, Just Salad and We Be Healthy. Order what fits your own needs; we do not rate the nutrition of any menu.

faq.q: Are there vegan options?
faq.a: Field of Greens' Tradition menu page names a vegan falafel wrap, and We Be Healthy's ordering site tags vegan dishes. Ask each restaurant about ingredients and preparation.

faq.q: Where can I eat gluten-free in Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: Berry Forkin' Good lists gluten-free granola in its bowls plus a gluten-free crepe and waffle, and says to call (772) 758-1069 if you have celiac disease. Always confirm with the restaurant.

faq.q: Do restaurants pay to be on this list?
faq.a: No. No listed business paid or is a partner. Each entry is on the list because its own site shows the menu, hours or address that we checked on 2026-10-27.

lists.title: Self-care and recovery in Port St. Lucie
lists.intro: Spa days, massage, yoga and nail care each have their own booking rules, so this list shows what each business's own site says. It also links the Florida state tool for checking that a salon or spa professional is licensed before you book.

faq.q: How do I check that a salon or spa professional is licensed?
faq.a: The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation has a free Verify a Licensee search on myfloridalicense.com where you can look up a business or a person by name. The site also has an Unlicensed Activity search.

faq.q: Where can I get a massage in Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: Sanctuary Spa (St. Lucie West), Natural Spa & Massage (Tradition area) and Massage Envy (St. Lucie West) all list massage. Our salon (listed once, below) offers nail services only.

faq.q: What should I know before a spa day?
faq.a: Sanctuary Spa's site asks guests to arrive about 15 minutes early, says children under 16 are not permitted unless receiving services, and lists a 24-hour notice for a la carte services and 48 hours for packages and Saturdays to avoid a 50 percent charge. Other spas set their own rules, so read before you book.

faq.q: Is there a gentle yoga class near Port St. Lucie?
faq.a: Down to Earth Yoga posts a weekly schedule that includes Gentle Yoga, YIN Restore and a Tai Chi series. Pricing and booking are on the studio's schedule-and-pricing page.

lists.title: 5Ks, Turkey Trots and a healthy holiday season in Port St. Lucie (Nov-Dec 2026)
lists.intro: Port St. Lucie's Thanksgiving morning 5K is the Turkey Trot at Tradition on Thursday, November 26, 2026, with the Freedom Isn't Free Run 5K on November 14 and the Centennial Athletics December Dash on December 12. Dates below come from official event or registration pages read on 2026-10-27 and re-read for the 5Ks on 2026-10-31; prices and start times can change.

faq.q: Is there a turkey trot in Port St. Lucie in 2026?
faq.a: Yes. The 9th annual Turkey Trot at Tradition is Thursday, November 26, 2026 with an 8:00 a.m. 5K start at Tradition Town Hall, Southwest Civic Lane. A second Thanksgiving 5K, the Pelican Yacht Club Turkey Trot, is in Fort Pierce at 7:15 a.m.

faq.q: Can I walk instead of run?
faq.a: The Turkey Trot at Tradition registration is for a '5K Race/Fun Run Walk' and says kids in strollers are welcome. The Freedom Isn't Free Run 5K lists walkers as welcome.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: The Turkey Trot at Tradition lists $40 for adults 19 and over through Oct. 26 and $45 from Oct. 27, with $30 for ages 18 and under. The Muster 5K is $35, the Pelican Turkey Trot $45 (rising after Nov. 22), and the December Dash $40. Check each page for current prices.

faq.q: Are there outdoor fitness classes in the cooler months?
faq.a: The City of Port St. Lucie says its outdoor Fitness Parks Pass classes (yoga in the parks, tai chi, Zumba and boot camps) return from November through April. A fall schedule had not been published when we checked.
